meta.generated_at_note: the newest of the input files' own stamps, not the time this ran
meta.title: Colorado county housing market direction and tax-credit rent edge
meta.geography: all 64 Colorado counties, and every town and CDP in geo-config (places)

calls.emerging: People or jobs are growing, at least two of permits, prices and rents are rising, and none is falling.
calls.steady: Neither rising nor falling on the rule below.
calls.softening: At least two of permits, prices and rents are falling.
calls.falling_demand: Household population and jobs are both shrinking.
calls.not_enough_data: Fewer than two market signals and no reading of both population and jobs.

meta.rule_order: not_enough_data, then falling_demand, then softening, then emerging, else steady: the first that applies is the call
meta.threshold_note: Thresholds are a reviewer's choice, not a standard. Prices are nominal: about 4% over three years is a fall after inflation. A signal between its two thresholds reads flat.

rent_edge.no_edge: The FMR is at or below the 60% AMI rent: a 60% unit can't charge its 60% rent.
rent_edge.thin: The 60% AMI rent is below the FMR by less than 10% of the FMR.
rent_edge.clear: The 60% AMI rent is below the FMR by 10% of the FMR or more.

meta.rent_edge_note: HUD FMR is the 40th-percentile gross rent of recent movers for the county's FMR area; several counties share a metro FMR, and non-metro counties often sit at the state non-metro level. CHFA 60% rents are gross and use HUD income limits, which hold rural counties at a national non-metro floor. Both are gross rents (utilities included). edge_pct is (FMR - 60% rent) / FMR: the discount a 60% unit offers against the market, as a share of the market rent, not the premium of the FMR over the 60% rent.

permits.source: U.S. Census Bureau Building Permits Survey (BPS), annual county and place files

price.source: FHFA annual Census-tract House Price Index

rent.source: Zillow Observed Rent Index (ZORI) — smoothed, seasonally adjusted

population.source: DOLA State Demography Office, county profiles (household population, households, net migration)

lihtc_rents.source: CHFA — 2026 Income Limit and Maximum Rent Tables for All Colorado Counties

permits_ytd.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Building Permits Survey, monthly year-to-date files
permits_ytd.note: context only: no call reads it. Homes permitted this year to date against the same months last year; change_pct is read only when each period has at least 50 homes

calls.emerging: Household population is growing, at least two of permits, prices and rents are rising, and none is falling.
calls.steady: Neither rising nor falling on the rule below.
calls.softening: At least two of permits, prices and rents are falling.
calls.falling_demand: Household population is shrinking by 0.25% a year or more, at least one of permits, prices and rents is falling or flat, and none is rising (towns only; CDPs have no DOLA series).
calls.not_enough_data: Fewer than two market signals and no household population reading, or a shrinking household population that no permit, price or rent reading confirms.
calls.second_home_shift: Household population is shrinking where seasonal homes are at least 20% of all homes: homes are leaving the year-round market, which is not falling demand.

places.rule_note: The county rule on what a place has. Price is one year of FHFA tract indexes modelled to the place, read against the county thresholds scaled to a year. No town-level jobs trend exists, so demand is household population alone; county_call is the county's call, for context. A town of a few hundred homes often has fewer than two market signals: that is not_enough_data, not a guess. With no jobs trend, a shrinking household population is falling_demand only when a market signal agrees (one falling or flat, none rising); where seasonal homes are 20% or more of homes (ACS, not graded unreliable) it is second_home_shift; unconfirmed it is not_enough_data; contradicted by a rising signal it is read on the market rule.
places.rule_order: not_enough_data (no demand reading), then for shrinking household population: second_home_shift, not_enough_data (no market signal), falling_demand (none rising), else on to softening, then emerging, else steady

seasonal_homes_source.source: ACS 5-year B25004_006 over B25001 (seasonal, recreational or occasional use)

population_source.source: Colorado State Demography Office, municipal population estimates (household population)
